# Civics Unit Objectives and Lesson Plan
Summit View Middle School | Grade 7 | Julia Duarte, Curtis Petrov, Daniel Brennan | 10/19/2026–10/30/2026

## Unit: The Constitution and the Branches of Government
Unit objective: By 10/30/2026, students will explain how the Constitution assigns and limits government power, citing at least two pieces of evidence from class sources in a short written response.

Students will see the unit objective on the opening slide each day, and Julia will read it aloud before instruction. Students will copy it into their civics notebooks.

## Lesson objectives
- 10/20, Lesson 1: Students will identify the three branches of the federal government and name one constitutional responsibility for each, earning at least 4 of 5 points on the exit ticket.
- 10/22, Lesson 2: Students will complete the source comparison activity using the Constitution and a classroom diagram.
- 10/26, Lesson 3: Students will explain one example of checks and balances in a paragraph that includes a claim and two accurate details.

For Lesson 1, the exit ticket has five items: identify the legislative, executive, and judicial branches; match each to one responsibility; and explain one way the branches limit one another. A score of 3/5 demonstrates mastery of the lesson objective.

## Project objective and communication
By 10/30, student pairs will create a one-page infographic showing how one constitutional power is divided or checked. Each infographic must include a claim, two cited details from the class sources, and a labeled example. Students will use the four branches of the federal government as categories for choosing a topic.

On 10/19, Curtis will distribute the project rubric and review its criteria with the class. Daniel will post the rubric and unit objective in the learning management system. Students will submit the infographic in class on 10/30; Julia will assess it with the same rubric shared at launch.

## Evidence of progress
Julia will review Lesson 1 exit tickets before Lesson 2 and group students who scored below 4/5 for a brief reteach. Lesson 3 paragraphs will be checked for a claim and two details before project work begins.
